messages:
mara_cs: FYI Omar from Quil reported a burst of 429s during their feature-flag flip in eu-west-1. Roughly 320 clients spiked within ~18s and init failed with 429s.

omar_client: Pasted sample from our edge: ```POST /v1/sdk/init HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
x-request-id: om-req-421
x-account-id: quil-prod
Response: 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 10
```

omar_client: At the moment of failures our edge emitted header `x-active-clients: 320` and we do short-lived worker restarts on deploy.

ethan_eng: Sounds like a classic init-stampede. Quick recommendations to give them now: 1) bump ephemeralTTL to something like 240s to avoid reauth churn; 2) add a small randomized splay on app startup (200-600ms) during rollouts; 3) stage the rollout (5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100%) and hold until auth QPS stabilizes; 4) ensure edge keeps connections alive / reuse (keepAlive/http2).

ethan_eng: Example short client shim to add jitter: ```// client bootstrap jitter
const jitterMs = Math.floor(Math.random()*600)
setTimeout(() => Redwood.init({ envKey: 'pk_live_quil', ephemeralTTL: 240 }), jitterMs)```

sdk-bot: Also note `prefetch` can increase parallel validation. If they use prefetch, suggest reducing prefetchConcurrency or disabling for the canary.

infra-signal: Infra traces show auth-validate QPS for account quil-prod peaked to ~3.8k at 2026-03-24T02:11Z and auth queue depth briefly increased. I can enable token-validation coalescing for their account (dedupe identical checks within 8s) behind a flag for a short window.

onboard-bot: Created ticket CS-#5422 "Quil init 429s during feature-flag flip". Assigned to ethan_eng, infra-signal. ETA for flag rollout: ~10m. Playbook: https://confluence.redwood/integration-playbooks/bootstrap-backpressure (internal).

omar_client: We'll flip TTL=240 and add the jitter on a 5% canary now. Rolling to 100% over 4m if green. Will report any x-request-id samples if 429s continue.

ethan_eng: If 429s persist after client changes, ask them to capture two failing `x-request-id` values plus their `x-client-conns` and `x-active-clients` headers at the time of failure. We'll correlate those with auth queue traces and consider expanding coalescing/windowed burst smoothing.

mara_cs: Logging this to Quil's account health note and will follow up when the canary finishes. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
